clue.text: Conveyance in wintertime? Endless dexterity required

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of the synonym is cut off

parts.note: sleight, as in sleight of hand, means dexterity

explanation.surface: A puzzle about needing nimble skill, perhaps to handle a winter vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleigh is a sledge drawn over snow, the classic vehicle of winter travel; the question mark flags a definition by example.

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a rank is a line, or row

explanation.surface: Someone brags about their rank or status.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to brag or gloat, from the cockerel's triumphant call.

clue.text: Six wearing fancy tunics in sports film

indicators.note: the anagrammed letters wear the numeral, so it goes inside them
fancy here means elaborately rearranged, an anagram signal

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Six players dressed up in fancy tunics in a film about sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The six players look like a rugby team in fancy kit, which suits the film's subject; 'Six' is really a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Invictus is the 2009 Clint Eastwood film about South Africa's 1995 Rugby World Cup victory.

clue.text: Tinned meat mostly for health resort

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Spam is a brand of tinned luncheon meat

explanation.surface: Serving tinned meat at a health resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a resort built around mineral springs, visited for wellbeing.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one's position or rank in life
second meaning: Paddington is a London railway terminus

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone phoning from Paddington; 'calling' means vocation or social position.
explanation.definitionFit: Station means both a social rank in life and a stopping place for trains, of which Paddington is an example.

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Robert Peel was a 19th-century British Prime Minister
the 's supplies an S

explanation.surface: A one-time Prime Minister is making a climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns PEELS upwards into SLEEP, which follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone out, or out cold, is unconscious, like a person in slumber.

clue.text: A good thing, only when healthy

parts.note: just means only
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
well means healthy

explanation.surface: Something being good only when one is in good health.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'just as well' says something is fortunate or a good job, an idiom of relief.

indicators.note: entering means going inside the following word

parts.note: a minster is a large church or cathedral, as in York Minster
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A senior politician arriving at a cathedral service.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister heads a government department, a high-ranking office holder.

clue.text: Girl beginning to tire carrying home musical instrument

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside

parts.note: Clare is a girl's name
in means at home

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A girl starting to get tired from carrying something home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to tire' joins the girl's name before 'carrying' acts, so the home piece goes inside the longer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a single-reed woodwind instrument.

indicators.note: ignored means left out of the word

parts.note: studious means academic, bookish
US is the United States, so American

explanation.surface: A studious American being overlooked in a workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is an artist's or craftsman's working room, much like a workshop.

clue.text: Fool about whilst playing electronic instrument

indicators.note: about means turned around, so read backwards

parts.note: a nit, or nitwit, is a fool

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are messed about with

parts.note: E is short for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: An idiot fooling about while playing an electronic instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'electronic' looks like it describes the instrument, but it only supplies a letter; 'about' and 'playing' work on separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin whistle is a simple six-holed metal flute used in folk music.

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A nervy win secures a double for a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin is one's double, a matching counterpart.

clue.text: Clan's leader, leader of tribe in Kent coastal area

parts.note: a thane was a Scottish clan chief or nobleman

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A clan chief and a tribal leader meet on the Kent coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clan's leader' looks like a first letter, but it is the whole word THANE; only 'leader of tribe' takes a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Thanet, the old Isle of Thanet, is the north-east corner of Kent, home to Margate and Ramsgate.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to better or surpass
third meaning: a lid or cap
fourth meaning: a ... is an upper-body garment, a sweater being one

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a spin bowler's cap and jumper; each word is a separate sense of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Top serves as verb for surpass, a spinning toy, a lid, and a garment for the upper body.

indicators.note: in means placed inside the following word

parts.note: to net something is to bag it; a net is also a bag
a Thermos is a vacuum flask

explanation.surface: A flask stuffed at the very bottom of a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Nethermost means lowest, the furthest below, from nether meaning lower.

clue.text: Facing it in the course of contest

indicators.note: in the course of means within, so the word goes inside

parts.note: to oppose is to contest

explanation.surface: Confronting a challenge during a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite means facing, positioned across from something.

parts.note: pro means in favour of, backing
a Test is an international match in cricket or rugby

explanation.surface: A player appeals in support of an international match.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest is a formal objection or appeal against a decision.

parts.note: rec is British short for recreation ground, a public playing field
an order is a booking or reservation

explanation.surface: A judge books a playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: In England and Wales a Recorder is a part-time judge sitting in the Crown Court.

indicators.note: nasty suggests something twisted out of its proper form

explanation.surface: A threat that is unpleasant at its root.
explanation.definitionFit: At heart is an idiom meaning fundamentally, in one's true nature.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to strangle or choke
second meaning: a ... controls fuel flow to an engine, like an accelerator

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as two car controls, the choke and accelerator; the first is really the verb to strangle.
explanation.definitionFit: Throttle is both a verb for strangling and the engine valve worked by the accelerator pedal.

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: a tier is a band or layer

explanation.surface: Briefly joining a band.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie two things is to fasten or connect them.

parts.note: up means ahead, as in a team being two goals up
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone ahead and drunk is still on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptight means tense and anxious, an informal word for being on edge.

clue.text: Team in bar gets a particular type of bottle

indicators.note: in means placed inside the following word

parts.note: to bar is to stop
a crew is a team

explanation.surface: A team at a pub gets a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but here it is the verb to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwtop bottle has a threaded cap that twists off, rather than a cork.

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: Thanking a poet for a knight's costume.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a short sleeveless tunic worn by knights over armour, bearing their arms.

indicators.note: in means placed inside the following word

parts.note: a rate is a class or grade, as in first-rate
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Telling the Spanish students in a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to narrate or recount it.

clue.text: Offer made by rival, no bluff

indicators.note: no means without, so these letters are removed

parts.note: a contender is a rival
a con is a bluff or trick

explanation.surface: A rival makes a straight offer with no bluffing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is a formal offer, a bid to supply goods or do work.

clue.text: Vehicle coming from market, heading west

indicators.note: in an across entry, heading west means running right to left, so backwards

parts.note: a mart is a market, as in a cattle mart

explanation.surface: A vehicle leaving a market and travelling west.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram is a passenger vehicle running on rails along the street.

clue.text: Minor celeb in golf becomes scathing

parts.note: a B-lister is a second-rank celebrity
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A minor celebrity playing golf turns cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: Blistering criticism is savagely harsh, so fierce it burns.

explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' suggests a sailor; 'man' is a chess piece and the board a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Rook is a verb for swindling and the name of a chess piece also called a castle.

clue.text: Tricky question plucked from quite a series

indicators.note: plucked from means taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A tricky question pulled from a long series of quizzes.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser is a puzzling problem, short for brain-teaser.

clue.text: Respected and admired husband everyone was in debt to

parts.note: H is the genealogy abbreviation for husband
all means everyone
owed means was in debt to, with 'was' joining

explanation.surface: A husband everyone owed money to was well thought of.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed means revered and held sacred, so greatly honoured.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pet form of Dorothy
second meaning: Americans call a full stop a period, and that mark is a small spot

explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Dorothy of The Wizard of Oz and her film era; 'period' is the American word for a full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Dot is a short form of the name and also the small round punctuation mark ending a sentence.
